# Experiments: cold read-in (4070 side)

All runs on the RTX 4070 12 GB, driver 610.88, memory clock 11,751 MHz under load. The 8 GB-like recipe pins the VRAM
line at 80,640 cells with q3_0 K/V (the 2060 line), so a deep prompt sits mostly in the host tail.

## T2a: prefill attention with 2 Q heads per column group (2026-10-16 04:08-04:31)

- **Plan** (kernel session, script header, before the run): kernel fork `t2-prefill` 2724a8349 = 0059 +
  `GGML_CUDA_FA_PREFILL_NCOLS2=2` (default 8). With GQA 6 the MMA kernel packs 8 Q-head columns per KV head, 2 of them
  padding; packing 2 heads x more tokens loads each K/V tile less often. Gates: FLASH_ATTN_EXT op tests 0 FAIL; answers
  byte-identical (d27_hash, 3 prompts, temp 0); then the prefill rate at 32k / 64k / 128k, alternated x2.
  Script: `scripts/t2a_ncols2.sh`.
- **Result:** op tests 3115/3115 in both arms. **Identity fails:** prompt 1 is identical, prompts 2 and 3 differ
  (prompt 2: 710 vs 592 tokens). Prefill, code prompt, both repeats agree: 32k 1,144 -> 1,170 tok/s (+2.5 %), the
  32k-64k chunk 857 -> 892 (+4.2 %), the 64k-128k chunk 618 -> 653 (+5.6 %). quick_tps reuses the cache between depths
  on one server, so only the 32k row is a cold read. Decode 2-5 % lower, confounded by the different outputs (draft
  acceptance). Receipt: `docs/receipts/prefill_ncols2_t2a.log`.
- **Cause (kernel session, corrected on #138 comment 6214090726):** ncols is the same in both arms (32 on Turing, 64 on
  Ada). The switch changes the number of Q tiles, and with it the stream-k split of the KV range across blocks, so the
  partial sums are combined in a different order. At best PPL-equal, not byte-identical. (A first reading, a change of
  the K/V tile length per softmax step, was wrong.)
- **P154 on the 2060 (sm_75, #138 comment 6213954510):** cold 64k 1.067x, cold 128k 1.110x, decode equal, the 4k code
  answer byte-identical. The declared rule asked for >= 10 % at 64k and 128k, so T2a as declared does not pass.
- **T2a-2** (a new plan, sm_75 only, #138 comment 6214090726): Q1 PPL + KL at 4k / 16k (KL <= 0.001, top-1 >= 99.5 %,
  PPL within +-0.2 %), then Q3 a cold 245k pair (>= 1.10x), then Q2 n24 / n28 / copies at 245k vs the 2060 default; stop
  at the first fail. Runs on the 2060.

## T2b-1: MMQ column-tile cap for the PTQ1_0 prefill matmuls, 4070 control (04:31-04:47)

- **Plan** (kernel session, script header, before the run): `-Xptxas -v` shows the PTQ1_0 MMQ instance spills on sm_75
  at J >= 64 (255 registers; J 128: 112-136 B, J 64: 24-72 B; none at J <= 48) and does not spill on sm_89. Engine `t2-prefill` 5bb256bb4 adds
  `GGML_CUDA_MMQ_MAX_J` and 12 PTQ1_0 prefill perf cases. The 4070 run is the control (no gain expected). Gates: G1 op
  tests 0 FAIL per J; G2 per-op perf sum >= 3 % better in both repeats; G3 prefill at 4k / 16k / 32k, same rule.
  Script: `scripts/t2b_maxj.sh` (the version as run; see the parse note).
- **Result:** G1 0 FAIL at J 128 / 64 / 48. G3, code prompt (4k cold; 16k and 32k are chunks at depth): J128 1,280 /
  1,212 / 1,042 tok/s, J64 1,124 / 1,064 / 933 (-12 %), J48 1,026 / 972 / 861 (-20 %). Answers change with J (stream-k
  split), as the header says. Receipt: `docs/receipts/prefill_mmq_maxj_t2b.log`.
- **Parse note:** the "G2 sum us/run" lines in the receipt hold ONE case only (m=12288 n=2048 k=5120): the CUDA graph
  log on stderr split each timing line. Recomputed from the saved logs over all 13 cases (kernel session, #138
  comment 6212813590): J128 20,412 / 20,459 us, J64 24,328 / 24,329 (+19 %), J48 27,580 / 27,617 (+35 %). The script was
  fixed for the 2060 run.
- **Reading:** a control as expected. The test that counts is the 2060 (sm_75), where J 48 removes the spills and J 64 reduces them.

## T1-a: slot save / restore, then the same request again (04:48-05:23)

- **Plan** (#138 comment 6212170839, before the run): bundle-20261016 bins (ab94810051), q3_0, line pinned 80,640,
  layer off; launcher = the product start-server.ps1 + one test-only line that passes `--slot-save-path`. Per depth:
  server 1 request A + save; server 2 (fresh) restore + the same request B; at 64k and 245k server 3 with no restore (C).
  Gates: G1 no error; G2 B == A (valid where C == A); G3 prompt_n after restore <= 512; G4 restore + prompt time <= 30 s
  at 245k. Scripts: `scripts/t1_slot.sh`, `scripts/t1_slot.py`.
- **Result: G3 fails.**

| depth | first read | save / file | restore | after restore: prompt_n / time | B = A |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | 64k | 68.2 s | 0.81 s / 1,051 MiB | 0.47 s | 65,732 / 68.3 s (all again) | yes (C = A) |
  | 128k | 177.8 s | 1.78 s / 1,939 MiB | 0.96 s | 130,608 / 177.8 s | yes |
  | 245k | 468.5 s | 3.29 s / 3,494 MiB | 1.72 s | 244,128 / 468.5 s | yes (C = A) |

- **Reading:** the files save and load at ~2 GB/s, but the repeat request reads the whole prompt again. The saved
  state ends after the 81 answer tokens; a repeat must roll back past them, and the 48 GDN layers keep a recurrent state
  that cannot roll back without a context checkpoint. The checkpoints are held in RAM and are not in the slot file.
  Receipts: `docs/receipts/t1_slot_restore.log` / `.jsonl`.

## T1-b: slot save / restore, then continue the conversation (05:24-05:47)

- **Plan** (#138 comment 6213052399, before the run): same recipe and root. Per depth: server 1 request 1 (A), save,
  then request 2 = request 1 + A as the assistant turn + a new question (D2, the in-memory continuation); server 2
  (fresh) restore + request 2 (B2); at 64k and 245k server 3 with no restore (C2, reported only). Gates: G1 no error;
  G2 B2 == D2 byte for byte; G3 prompt_n of request 2 after restore <= 1,024; G4 restore + prompt time <= 30 s at 245k.
  Scripts: `scripts/t1b_slot.sh`, `scripts/t1b_slot.py`.
- **Result: all gates pass.**

| depth | first read | save / file | restore | request 2 after restore: prompt_n / time | B2 = D2 | C2 (full read) |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | 64k | 68.2 s | 0.82 s / 1,051 MiB | 0.49 s | 32 / 0.28 s | yes | 65,845 tokens, 68.4 s, same answer |
  | 128k | 177.7 s | 1.84 s / 1,939 MiB | 0.93 s | 32 / 0.32 s | yes | not run |
  | 245k | 468.4 s | 3.30 s / 3,494 MiB | 1.69 s | 32 / 0.52 s | yes | 244,241 tokens, 468.7 s, same answer |

- **Reading:** the existing slot save / restore works with the tiered KV cache and the GDN / conv states when the next
  request extends the saved tokens: at 245k, 2.2 s against a 468 s read on this card (the 2060 reads 245k in ~1,695 s;
  the file is the same size there). T1-a's failure is the rollback case only (the same request again, or an edited
  history). Receipts: `docs/receipts/t1b_slot_continue.log` / `.jsonl`.
- **Next (proposal on #138):** a launcher switch for `--slot-save-path`; automatic save after large requests to a file
  named by a hash of the tokens, and a restore of the longest saved prefix on a fresh server; context checkpoints in the
  slot file for the rollback case.

## The 2060's T1 runs (by the 8 GB tester, #138; receipts in its receipts/p15x/)

- **P153** (T1-b on the 2060, thinking off): restore + continue 64k 1.12 s + 0.73 s, 128k 1.93 + 0.82, **245k 3.41 + 1.82 s
  = 5.2 s instead of a 1,689 s read**; answers byte-identical. Thinking on: the template drops the reasoning from the
  history, the request diverges inside the saved answer and reads everything again.
- **P155 / P155b** (layer T1-c v1 / v2): v2's save point (the end of the last message, before the generation prompt)
  restores in both thinking modes. After a restore, a multi-ubatch continuation crashed (`ggml-cuda.cu:109`,
  intermittent) or read at ~12 tok/s.
- **P157 / P157b:** the slowdown is deterministic and only on a fresh server; at 64k: defaults 165.6 s for 3,969 new
  tokens, `BONSAI_LOOKUP=0` the same, **`BONSAI_SPEC=0` 18.7 s**. Cause: the slot file held the target context only; the
  MTP draft context started empty in a fresh process. (The 4070 never showed the slowdown with the same server code.)

## T1-e / T1-f / T1-g: the 2060's restore failure does not reproduce on the 4070 (08:32-11:04)

- **T1-e** (8 GB preset, 131k, a 5,478-token new turn; arms default / calib file moved aside / `BONSAI_SPARSE=0`; plan on
  #138 before the run): restore 0.88-0.90 s, new turn 11.1-11.2 s (= in memory 11.3 s), answer equal, 0 CUDA errors in
  all arms. Receipt `t1e_restore_long.log`.
- **T1-f** (the same with `GGML_CUDA_GDN_MMA_DISABLE=1`: the recurrent GDN kernel with K 2 snapshot slots, the sm_75
  path): restore 0.94 s + 11.5 s, no error, answer equal. The recurrent-GDN theory is out on sm_89. Receipt
  `t1f_recurrent_gdn.log`.
- **T1-g** (VRAM trace; GPU Process Memory counters): a restored server does not hold more VRAM (peak 8,019 vs 8,049
  MiB; shared 2,604 MiB in both = the pinned host tail). Part 2, a torch ballast leaving 7.06 GB free: a plain cold
  read crawled at ~40 tok/s (shared +950 MiB: the Windows sysmem fallback spill), so it was stopped (no restore-specific
  reading possible). Side finding for the backlog: VRAM that grows after launch silently slows the server 10-20x.
  Receipt `t1g_vram.log`.

## T1-h: the MTP draft-context sidecar (11:37-11:49)

- **Fix** (kernel session, kernel fork `product-slotdraft` **303f01131** = product-0059 + two server commits): the slot
  save also writes the draft context's sequence state to `<file>.draft`; restore loads it; with no sidecar it clears
  the draft sequence and warns.
- **Plan** (#138, before the run): both files written; restore logs `draft context state restored`; answer = in memory;
  speed within 10 %; without the sidecar the warning; no CUDA error.
- **Run 1 void:** "restored (12 bytes)": the first commit made only the header probe call of
  `llama_state_seq_load_file`, so nothing was loaded (fixed in 303f01131). Receipt `t1h_slotdraft_run1_void.log`.
- **Rerun: all gates pass.** `.draft` 15,007,796 B; `draft context state restored (15007796 bytes)`; restore 1.00 s +
  11.22 s, answer = in memory; without the sidecar `no draft context state ... (the draft context starts empty)`, same
  answer; 0 errors. The 4070 never showed the slow path, so the 2060's P158 is the test of the speed fix. Receipt
  `t1h_slotdraft.log`.

## T3: block-sparse prefill attention (kernel session's plans on #138; 4070 runs 07:40-12:49)

| step | what | result | receipt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Q0 | emulation, per 64-query tile, keep 1/4 of the far pages; n24 / n28 / copies at 245k vs dense | **fail**: n24 loses vault 15 (gains 14); stopped after n24 | `t3_q0_prefill_sparse.log` |
| Q0a | per query, 1/4 | **fail**: n24 loses vault 6 | `t3_q0ab_prefill_sparse.log` |
| Q0b | per 64-query tile, **1/2** | **pass** on all three sets: n24 24/24 (gain 14), n28 27/28 (miss 15 = dense; gains 19, 24), copies 19 / 20 = dense | `t3_q0ab_*`, `t3_q0b2_prefill_sparse.log` |
| S0 | 8k KL of the speed path (two void runs: a missing tool DLL; the RAM guard stopped a 16k base at 31 GB) | keep-all arm KLD 0 / top 100 % (correct); 1/2: KLD 0.0027, top 97.8 %; 1/4: 0.011, 96.1 % | `t3_s0_kl.log` |
| S1 | first speed path (+ the per-tile skip map, 5225e138c), cold reads | part 1: the map changes nothing (1/2 with and without it: KLD 0.002740); slower than dense: 128k 0.79x, 245k 0.64x (the per-(page, query) score kernel) | `t3_s1_speed.log` |
| S2 | tiled score kernel | 128k **1.07x** (rule 1.10x: not met); scores 42.8 -> 2.7 ms per op | `t3_s2_speed.log` |
| S3 | split by stage, 245k | **245k 1.159x** (526.0 -> 609.8 tok/s, 463.7 -> 400.0 s): rule 1.15x **met**; to the 2060 for a speed probe | `t3_s3_split.log` |
| S4 / S5 | per-tile skip map: diagnostics | the map is built (mean visible 0.667); Nsight Compute: -21.8 % kernel time per deep launch; S4's -7 % was diluted by dense ops below the VRAM line | `t3_s4_vis.log`, `t3_s5_ncu.log` |

Q0 / Q0a / Q0b ran the quality-only emulation (a per-query mask on the dense kernel), not the speed path; the speed
path's own item gates are still open (2060). The "T3 engage lines: 0" in Q0 means a filtered INFO line; the sparse op counter showed 5,121 prefill-only ops.

## P152 (2060): the full window is free up to 128k

BONSAI_CTX 131,072 vs 262,144, alternated x2: decode within 1 % at 4k / 64k / 96k / 128k (52.6 / 40.5 / 35.2 / 22.4
tok/s), prefill equal. Docs can say: the full 262k window costs nothing up to 128k; only filling it is slow.

## T3 after S5: the 2060 probe and the gates (2026-10-16 evening)

- **P159** (2060, t3-prefill 0f7a8e0ce, 8 GB preset defaults, T2 off): cold 128k 589.3 -> 537.9 s (1.095x), **cold
  245k 1,693.3 -> 1,384.8 s (1.223x)**; the speed rule (>= 1.15x at 245k) met; 0 CUDA errors.
- **Gates** (kernel session, #138, before the runs): G0 4k hashes T3 = dense on both rigs; G1 / G2 245k items on the
  2060 / 4070 (copies n 20, needles n 24 / n 28), no lost item; G3 160k items; G4 speed. Bins: kernel fork
  `product-t3` 0ef8c83d9 (= the bundle-20261016b engine + the T3 chain, off by default); T3 arm
  `GGML_CUDA_FA_PREFILL_SPARSE=0.5`, `QTILE=64`, `STAT=1`; dense = the same bins, env unset; the launcher's product
  env (`BONSAI_8GB=1`, q3_0, line 80,640).
- **4070 (19:40-20:34):** G0 pass (dense = T3 = `1370fc25030ce635`). **G2 fail:** copies 19 / 20 both; n28 28/28 both;
  **n24 dense 24/24, T3 22/24 (loses vault 14 and vault 15)**. T3 engaged on every T3 server; 0 CUDA errors. The
  product-env dense reference (n24 24/24, n28 28/28) is better than the older pinned-dense reference (23/24, 25/28)
  that Q0b was judged against; vaults 14 / 15 are the threshold items that fixed 1/8 decode and D30 DELTA 4 also lost.
  Receipt `docs/receipts/t3_gates_4070.log` / `.jsonl`.
- **Decision (kernel session):** T3 is **closed as a default**: 1.22x cold 245k on the 2060, but it loses n24 vaults
  14 / 15 against the product dense reference on the 4070 (G2). It stays opt-in on the kernel fork, with no release
  work; the 2060's G1 / G3 / G4 were dropped.

# Cold read-in on 8 GB, 2026-10-16

Marguerite found that the standby generator behind the east annex had been filled with kerosene by mistake.

Goal (issue #138): make deep context usable on 8 GB. After bundle-20261016 the RTX 2060 SUPER reads a cold 64k prompt
in ~206 s, 128k in ~595 s and 245k in ~1,695 s (P143 / P150). A fit of the prefill rates gives ~2.4 ms per token of
fixed work (PTQ1_0 matmul ~70 %, GDN, the rest) plus attention that grows with depth: the fixed part alone is ~310 s
at 128k. The plan, the scoreboard and the four tracks are on #138:

| track | what | status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| T1 avoid | persistent prefix cache on disk: save the KV + GDN / conv states, restore in seconds | **T1-b pass** (4070: 245k in 2.2 s instead of 468 s; 2060 P153: 5.2 s instead of 28 min); launcher switch `BONSAI_SLOT_SAVE_PATH` merged; MTP draft-context sidecar (product-slotdraft 303f01131) passes T1-h, P158 on the 2060 next |
| T2 exact speed | FA prefill tiles, PTQ1_0 MMQ tuning, op fusion | T2a not exact as built (waits for P154 on the 2060); T2b is a control on the 4070, the real test is sm_75 |
| T3 sparse prefill | block-sparse attention for prompt chunks from the page bounds | closed as a default: 1.22x cold 245k on the 2060 (P159), but loses n24 vaults 14 / 15 against the product dense reference on the 4070 (G2); opt-in on the kernel fork |
| T4 fewer tokens | token selection before the full pass | feasibility |

Each plan was written before its run (the plan comments on #138 carry the times). Results: [EXPERIMENTS.md](EXPERIMENTS.md).
Scripts as run: `scripts/` (user paths replaced by `<user>`). The 2060's runs (P-numbers) are logged on #138 / #105.

# Experiments D01-D20

Format per entry: **question**, **gate** (and where it was declared), **setup** (hardware, engine commit, root, env,
script), **result**, **verdict**, **receipts**. RTX 4070 12 GB, 12 GB recipe (262k window, q8_0 KV, tiered cache,
MTP + lookup drafting, layer off) unless stated. "Mean decode" is `bench/quick_tps.py`'s mean over its code / prose /
bash items (400 tokens each). Retrieval: `bench/needle_depth.py` (12 facts) and `bench/code_needle.py` (exact copies
of 10 short Python functions from `artifacts/eval/pycode.raw`).

---

## D01 Side request re-reads the whole prompt (2026-10-10 09:30-11:51)

- **Question.** Coding agents send short side requests (titles, summaries) between turns. With one slot, does the next
  turn re-read the whole prompt?
- **Gate.** None (diagnosis). Fix gate declared in chat: turn 2 reuses the cached prompt.
- **Setup.** 120k-token prompt, then a 25-146-token side request, then turn 2 (`bench/side_request.py`,
  `bench/side_ab.sh`). Arms: `np1` (product), `np2` (`BONSAI_SLOTS=2`, unified KV, idle-slot cache off), `np2keep`
  (same + `LLAMA_SLOT_KEEP_TOKENS=4096`, engine `87e2ac160`).
- **Result.**

| arm | turn 2 tokens read | cached | turn 2 wall |
  | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
  | np1 | 119,995 | 121 | 178.8 s |
  | np2 | 120,116 | 0 | 232.3 s |
  | np2keep | **19** | **120,097** | **0.7 s** |

The first np2keep run (11:16) is void: two test chains ran on the GPU at the same time (out of memory).
- **Verdict.** Cause found: the side request takes the only slot (np1), or the similarity rule gives it the deep slot
  (np2). `LLAMA_SLOT_KEEP_TOKENS` keeps a deep slot for its conversation. Prototype only; see D02 for its cost.
- **Receipts.** `docs/receipts/side_ab.log`, `docs/receipts/side_ab.jsonl`.

## D02 Cost of a second slot (2026-10-10 12:24-12:32)

- **Question.** What does `-np 2` cost at 32k?
- **Gate.** None (measurement).
- **Setup.** `bench/slots_prefill.sh`, code item at 32k, `BONSAI_VRAM_MARGIN=1300` in all arms.
- **Result.** Mean decode / prefill: np1 85.5 / 1045.5, np1 unified 86.0 / 1041.8, np2 not unified 12.6 / 161.4
  (broken), **np2 unified 71.9 / 819.9 (-16 % / -22 %)**, np1 again 86.1 / 1040.6.
- **Verdict.** Unified KV is required for two slots; the remaining -16 % is unexplained (open). D01's fix is not
  shipped until this cost is understood.
- **Receipts.** `docs/receipts/slots_prefill.log`.

## D03 Sparse host-tail reads: retrieval, emulation (2026-10-10 11:23-12:12)

- **Question.** If each query reads only the top pages of the host tail (Quest page bounds), does retrieval hold?
- **Gate.** Declared in chat and #21: needles equal to dense.
- **Setup.** Engine `f5f273aed` (emulation: every host row still read, the mask hides the rest). 160k, VRAM line
  pinned at 32,768 cells (`BONSAI_KV_VRAM_CELLS`), graphs off, f16 mask, `GGML_CUDA_FA_SPARSE=B,64,1024`
  (`bench/needle_ab.sh`).
- **Result.** Needles: dense 12/12, B = 8192 12/12, B = 4096 12/12. (The first dense arm at 11:23 did not start:
  health = 0; rerun at 11:51.)
- **Verdict.** Pass at both budgets.
- **Receipts.** `docs/receipts/needle_ab.log`, `.jsonl`.

## D04 Sparse host-tail reads: exact code copies, emulation (2026-10-10 13:24-13:49)

- **Question.** Does exact recall of code hold? Needles are easy; copying a function needs every token.
- **Gate.** Declared in chat: copies equal to dense.
- **Setup.** As D03, `bench/code_needle_ab.sh`.
- **Result.** Exact copies: dense 10/10, B = 8192 **10/10**, B = 4096 8/10.
- **Verdict.** B = 8192 (page 64) passes; B = 4096 fails. B = 8192 is the budget from here on.
- **Receipts.** `docs/receipts/code_needle_ab.log`, `.jsonl`.

## D05 Sparse reads: KL on wikitext (2026-10-10 10:02-11:16, then 12:54-13:23)

- **Question.** KL divergence of sparse vs dense logits at depth.
- **Gate.** None declared.
- **Setup.** `llama-perplexity --kl-divergence-base` on wikitext-2 with a 64k-class window, one chunk (the first
  attempt with three chunks wrote 16 GB of logits per chunk and was restarted with `--chunks 1`); the exact flags of this
  early run were not kept, because `bench/sparse_kl.sh` was rewritten afterwards (13:49) with safe defaults.
- **Result (one chunk).**

| arm | mean KLD | same top-1 | max KLD | 99.9 % KLD |
  | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
  | dense base | | | | |
  | B = 8192 | 0.002998 | 97.720 % | 0.624 | 0.155 |
  | B = 4096 | 0.008089 | 96.356 % | 3.135 | 0.370 |

Base perplexity 7.9458 +/- 0.11443. Two lines at 10:21 are void (an old instance ran against a deleted base file).
  The follow-up runs at 64k (wikitext and Python source, 12:54-13:23) froze the PC twice (12:55 and about 13:10). From
  the Windows event log: low virtual memory naming `llama-perplexity`; the KL base keeps about n_ctx / 2 x 248,320 vocab
  x 4 bytes = ~32 GB of logits on a 32 GB machine. A rerun at the safe size (`-c 16384`) wrote nothing usable.
- **Verdict.** Consistent with D03 / D04: B = 8192 is close to dense, B = 4096 lossier. One chunk only, so it is a
  check, not a gate. Lasting changes: `tools/ramguard.ps1` (kills `llama-server` / `llama-perplexity` when free commit
  < 6 GB or free RAM < 1.5 GB) in every heavy script, and the rule "estimate a run's RAM first; KL at most 16k context
  with this vocab".
- **Receipts.** `docs/receipts/sparse_kl.log`.

## D06 Vec kernel skips fully masked tiles (2026-10-10, `346b123b5`)

- **Question.** Can the decode attention kernel skip a 128-cell tile whose mask is `-inf` for every cell and column,
  so unselected host pages are not read?
- **Gate.** Exactness: all `FLASH_ATTN_EXT` op tests pass.
- **Result.** `test-backend-ops -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT -b CUDA0`: 3007 ok, 0 fail.
- **Verdict.** Exact; kept. (Its 128-cell size later turned out too coarse for 64-cell pages on 2-query steps, D17.)
- **Receipts.** `docs/receipts/sparse_speed.log` (first line).

## D07 Sparse decode speed, first fast builds (2026-10-10 18:55-20:23)

- **Question.** Does reading only the kept pages speed up decode at 192k and 250k?
- **Gate.** None (measurement).
- **Setup.** `bench/sparse_speed.sh`, 12 GB recipe's own VRAM line. Arms: dense as shipped (graphs on, packed mask),
  dense-fair (graphs off, f16 mask), sparse `8192,256,1024` fast. Lookup off: engine `c084831aa`; lookup on: engine
  `71371d4cb` (fast path up to 64 queries, page staging).
- **Result.** Mean decode at 192k / 250k:

| arm | lookup off | lookup on |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | dense as shipped | 19.8 / 12.3 | 19.7 / 12.7 |
  | dense-fair (graphs off) | 22.8 / 13.4 | |
  | sparse | 21.5 / 13.5 | 14.4 / 9.2 |

- **Verdict.** No gain; slower with lookup. Two findings came out of it: dense-fair beat dense as shipped by 15 %,
  which led to the CUDA graphs finding (patch 0053, `docs/research/release-20261011/`); and the sparse arms paid a host
  sync per K write (fixed in `2f47c38b7`, D09) and read masked tiles (D11).
- **Receipts.** `docs/receipts/sparse_speed.log`.

## D08 Cached page bounds after a deep prompt edit (2026-10-10 18:55-19:07)

- **Question.** The fast path caches page bounds per K tensor. After a deep prompt edit, are they stale?
- **Gate.** Declared in chat: 0 stale-bound ops with tracking on.
- **Setup.** `bench/sparse_edit.sh`, engine `71371d4cb` with `GGML_CUDA_FA_SPARSE_CHECK=1` (recomputes all bounds every

  and the page selection is unchanged (1 KiB per host cell at page 64: 114 / 196 MiB). The first fill in chunks of
  `GGML_CUDA_FA_SPARSE_FILL_CELLS` cells (default 16384): 32 MiB at any depth.

  12/12, decode within 3 % of `root-sparse11`; peak VRAM lower than `root-sparse11` in the same arm.

| gate | `root-sparse11` (before) | `root-sparse12` (`8d5b862fc`) |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `FLASH_ATTN_EXT` op tests | | 3005/3005 |
  | `sparse_edit` 160k, stale ops (base / edit / again) | | track 0 / 0 / 0; notrack control 0 / 192 / 192 |
  | 160k exact copies / needles | 10/10, 12/12 | 10/10, 12/12 |
  | peak `memory.used` (8 GB-like layout, line 32,768) | 9,747 MiB | **9,356 MiB (-391 MiB)** |
  | mean decode (code / prose / bash) | 25.5 (29.3 / 20.4 / 26.9) | 27.6 (31.6 / 22.0 / 29.0) |

The memory drop matches the analysis at this depth (host tail 126,720 cells: tables 256 -> 128 MiB, first fill

## D26c / D26e Two-level page bounds (2026-10-14 12:28-13:16)

- **Question.** Can the page bounds take almost no VRAM (D26a: the 64k cost is the VRAM line)? Design (`sparse-d26`
  `71dcac6fe`): coarse f16 bounds per superpage stay in VRAM; the fine int8 page bounds move to pinned host memory.
  Per op the GPU scores superpages, keeps the top M x what the budget needs, then reads only their fine bounds over
  PCIe. `GGML_CUDA_FA_SPARSE_OVERLAP=1` (debug) also runs the one-level selection and logs the share of its
  non-recent pages the two-level path keeps.
- **Gate.** Declared in the script headers: overlap >= 99 % and `_pydecimal.py` `_convert_other` copied exactly.
- **Setup.** root `root-psparse-d26`, B 12288 floor + FRAC 1/16, line 32,768, graphs on, packed mask on, driver 610.88.
- **D26c (super 16 pages, M 4 and M 8; 245k and 200k).** The script escaped the dollar in the log paths, so each arm's
  logs went to one shared file one directory up and the 245k arms' logs were overwritten. The recovered 200k M 4 log:
  two-level on ("bounds int8 two-level", 176 MiB counted), overlap 67.6-68.0 % (worst op 50.1 %). The item failed in
  all three arms. Rejected: 16-page superpage bounds are too loose to rank.
- **D26e (200k, fixed log paths).**

| superpage | M | overlap | worst op | item |
  | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
  | 4 pages | 4 | 87.6 % | 78.5 % | exact |
  | 4 pages | 8 | **98.9 %** | 95.7 % | exact |
  | 16 pages | 8 | 91.4 % | 81.5 % | exact |

- **Verdict: two-level closed.** It works (superpage 4 / M 8: overlap 98.9 %, the item exact), but it does not pay.
  The coarse bounds are f16 in this build, so superpage 4 costs 256 B per host cell in VRAM (about 52 MiB at 213k host
  cells): half of the int8 one-level reserve, not a tenth. And M 8 reads the fine bounds of keep x 8 = 1,536 of 2,552
  pages per op at 200k (about 60 %), about 66 MB per token: about 5.5 ms per token on the 2060's PCIe 3.0, about +8 %
  at 245k, with a larger M needed for 99 %. So it gives back at depth (where users opt in) what it saves on the line at
  shallow depth. Sparse stays opt-in with the full int8 reserve; the 2060's P137 measures how much of its 7-8 % at 64k
  is the line on PCIe 3.0. No D26f.
- **Clock note.** These scripts logged `clocks.max.memory`, which always reads 10501 MHz. The memory overclock was off
  at 04:11 (10251 MHz under load) and on by about 12:24 (11751 MHz under load at 13:09). Overlap and copies do not
  depend on the clock.
- **Receipts.** `docs/receipts/sparse_twolevel_d26c.log` (with a correction note), `d26c_200000_m4.server.log`,
  `sparse_twolevel_d26e.log`.

## D30 plan: adaptive sparse page budget (written 2026-10-16, before the run; issue #138)

- **Question.** q3_0 needs FRAC 1/4 for dense quality (D26h-3); 1/8 gave the 2060 1.44x at 245k (P143), 1/4 only
  +10 %. Can a per-row budget keep the 1/8 speed at the 1/4 quality?
- **Mechanism** (kernel fork `sparse-d30` 2295d37d0 = 0059 + `GGML_CUDA_FA_SPARSE_FLOOR_FRAC` + `_DELTA` +
  `_KEPTSTAT`): each row keeps max(B, floor x tail) pages, then adds pages up to the FRAC cap only while their bound is
  within DELTA logits of the row's best. Peaked rows stay near the floor, flat rows go to the cap. KEPTSTAT prints the
  mean kept share every 256 sparse decode ops.
- **Setup.** 4070, q3_0, 245k, line pinned 80,640 (the 2060 line), sparse forced (auto off), graphs and packed mask on,
  cap 1/4 + floor 1/8, DELTA 4 and 8; per arm one fresh server per set: needle_depth n 24, n 28, code_needle n 20
  (`plans/d30_adaptive.sh`).
- **Gate (declared before the run):** an arm passes when every item equals dense on the three sets (dense, D26h-1e /
  D26h-3: n24 misses 14; n28 misses 15, 19, 24; copies 19 strict / 20 lenient) AND its mean kept share is below 0.20.
- **Amendment (2026-10-16 03:31, issue #138).** After P149 part 1 (the 2060 keeps vault 16 at 1/8, the 4070 loses it),

# Outside work considered (2026-10-10 / 11)

Techniques from papers, upstream llama.cpp and other inference projects, surveyed while planning this round, with what
we did about each. Numbers are the sources' own (not reproduced here unless an experiment ID is given).

## Long-context decode with a cache in host memory

| technique (source) | mechanism | what we did |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quest (arXiv 2406.10774) | per-page min/max of K bounds each page's score; read the top pages only | implemented (`fa-sparse-proto`); D03, D04, D08, D10, D16 |
| FreeKV (arXiv 2505.13109) | choose pages from the previous step's query so the copy can be prefetched | not built; candidate if the selection cost shows in op timing |
| Whole-context selection with sinks (Quest-style, applied to all cells) | attention work follows the budget, not the context length | `SINKS`; rejected at page 256 (D11), retry queued |
| CPU attention for the host part, merged by log-sum-exp (HGCA arXiv 2507.03153, ScoutAttention arXiv 2603.27138) | GPU attends the VRAM part, CPU the host part | measured earlier on the 8 GB rig: a 6-core CPU needs ~110 ms per layer for 192k rows (`docs/8GB.md`); not pursued |
| Low-bit KV for the host tail (KIVI arXiv 2402.02750, rotated 3-4-bit KV in community llama.cpp forks) | fewer bytes per cell over PCIe | not built; quality reports for 3-bit are mixed |
| "Sparse V" skip (community llama.cpp forks) | skip V work where softmax weights are ~0 | `GGML_CUDA_FA_V_SKIP`; exact, no gain here (D12) |
| Eviction (SnapKV, PyramidKV) | drop cells permanently after the prompt | not tried: cannot be recalled, breaks exact copies |
| Engine paging with a model-native sparse indexer (one MoE engine whose full-attention layers pick 2,048 cells per step) | page cache works because the model reads few cells | not portable to dense attention; our sparse selection is the approximate equivalent |

## Long-context prefill

| technique (source) | mechanism | what we did |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Block-sparse prefill (MInference arXiv 2407.02490, FlexPrefill 2502.20766, XAttention 2503.16428, RBS-Attention 2609.20971) | each query block attends to selected key blocks | MMA tile skip built; sparse prefill with Quest page bounds lost exact copies (D10) |
| Selector ablation (RBS-Attention) | at equal density, Quest-style bounds score like other selectors; cumulative-mass thresholds and always-kept sink / local / column blocks matter more | informs any retry |
| Speculative prefill (arXiv 2502.02789) | a small model scores tokens; the big model prefills only the important spans | not tried: lossy for every later turn of an agent session |
| Chunked gated-delta-net prefill (ggml-org/llama.cpp#29353) | MMA kernel for the delta rule over chunks, BF16 hi/lo split, fp32 state | ported with three changes for this model (D14) |
| fp16 accumulation or INT8 for QK in the attention kernel (SageAttention arXiv 2411.10958) | GeForce tensor cores run fp32 accumulation at half rate; our QK accumulates in fp32, PV in fp16 | not built; SageAttention itself does not support head dim 256 or Turing |
| Larger prefill micro-batches (several community guides) | fewer reads of the prefix per prompt | measured: 512 is best here (D13) |

# Depth research: report (2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14)

Speed past the VRAM line on one RTX 4070 12 GB (PCIe 4.0), with the RTX 2060 SUPER 8 GB (PCIe 3.0) runs from #21 /
#22. Paired arms on the same binary where possible; gates declared before results (see README for where).
Experiment entries: `EXPERIMENTS.md`; machine-readable: `runs.jsonl` (with `gpu_h`, RTX 4070 hours from receipt timestamps: 17.4 h for this folder).

## Bottom line

1. **The largest gain was a configuration fault, not a kernel.** The tier prefetch (copy engine moves the next
   attention op's host rows while the current op computes) only ran without a CUDA graph, and the launcher keeps CUDA
   graphs on. Found from D07 (graphs off beat the shipped setup by 15 % at 192k), isolated and gated as patch 0053 (shipped in bundle-20261011, 2026-10-13):
   +25 % decode at 192k on 12 GB, +8 to +16 % past the line on 8 GB, nothing lost below the line. Isolation, gates and
   release: `docs/research/release-20261011/`.
2. **Sparse reads of the host tail shipped as an opt-in for 8 GB: patch 0055, bundle-20261014, `BONSAI_SPARSE=1`.**
   Gated on both cards with CUDA graphs on (0053 turns them off per graph past the line) and the packed mask on:
   RTX 2060 SUPER 160k 10.6 -> 17.5 tok/s (1.65x), 245k 6.3 -> 13.7 (2.17x), exact copies and needles equal to dense
   at 160k / 200k / 245k (P135, P136); RTX 4070 8 GB-like line 160k 14.4 -> 24.1 (R05b), 245k 8.8 -> 20.4 (R04).
   What it took:
   - the kernels skip what the mask hides at the page's own granularity (D06, D10, D17);
   - the sparse-only VRAM counted in the launcher's line: f16 then int8 page bounds rounded outward, 514 B per host
     cell, a chunked first fill, 64 MiB headroom from a 245k trace (D18, D22, release-20261014);
   - a budget that grows with depth: max(12288, host tail / 16). A fixed 8192 lost an exact copy at 245k, 1/16 alone
     lost one at 200k on a 20-item set (D22c, R04b-R04d);
   - below `MIN_HOST` the op is the dense op, prefetch included (P118 routing fix).
   Opt-in, not default: the bounds reserve shortens the VRAM line, which costs ~8 % at 64k on the 2060 (P123, P127)
   and ~2.6 % on the 4070 (D26a). The engine itself adds nothing at an equal line (D26a).
3. **The kernel must skip what the mask hides, or sparse is slower than dense.** The first sparse builds read every
   masked host tile in place (D07, D09, D10: 9.1 vs 13.6 tok/s), because draft-verify steps run the MMA kernel, which
   had no skip. Each kernel path needs its own skip at the page's own granularity (D06, D10, D17).
4. **Quality fails first where selection is aggressive:** sparse prefill (D10: 8/10 copies) and selection over the VRAM
   part (D11: 7/12 needles) are rejected at the tested settings.
5. **Chunked gated-delta-net prefill shipped: patch 0054, bundle-20261013** (D14): prefill +3 to +7 % on RTX 30 / 40,
   decode unchanged, perplexity +0.024 %; HumanEval 158 vs 160 (two long-thinking flips, trajectory drift); not taken
   on RTX 20 (P116).
6. **What did not help the sparse path:** per-head normalized ranking (D23: it moves the needed pages down), a
   per-layer budget (D25: the middle layers carry mid-context items too), two-level bounds in host memory (D26c / D26e:
   98.9 % overlap at 256-cell superpages, but the per-token PCIe read cancels the line it saves).
7. **No gain:** V skip (D12), a larger prefill micro-batch (D13: 512 is best), a third-party template for tool work
   (D15). **KL at depth (D05):** one chunk measured (B = 8192: mean KLD 0.0030, same top-1 97.7 %); the longer runs froze the PC and produced the RAM guard rule.

## Lessons for the next model

- **Count every device allocation of a new path in the VRAM budget.** The 245k sparse loss (P107) was not in the
  kernel: ops that sparse does not touch got 2.5-24x slower once the card went over its total. Op timing finds this
  shape (slow ops that did not change); a VRAM trace across the first decode step confirms it.
- **Measure before building.** The op timing (D09) and a plain graphs-off arm (D07) explained more than the kernel
  prototypes did. Next time, run a graphs on/off and per-op timing pair at depth first.
- **Every new path needs a "did it engage" log line.** The chunked gated-delta-net kernel ran zero times in the first
  A/B (D14), and the sparse path was invisible in the server log at INFO level. Make such lines WARN or always on.
- **Test the 8 GB card early.** The 8 GB-like layout on the 4070 does not reproduce the 2060's decode shape: MTP
  tail 1 gives 2-query steps that run a different kernel.
- **A gate that the dense arm cannot pass is not a gate.** R04 said "copies 10/10"; dense itself missed an item at 200k
  (R04b). Compare sparse to dense on the same items, and use 20 items where a single miss decides.
- **Check that a debug run's logs exist before reading its verdict.** D26c looked void: a shell escape (`\$NAME` in
  double quotes) put the server logs one directory up.
- **Plan files.** Gates were declared in chat or on issues, not frozen in `<ID>-plan.json`. Write the plan file
  first next time.
- **RAM.** Estimate a run's host memory before starting it. Keep `tools/ramguard.ps1` in every heavy script. KL
  divergence with this 248k vocab only at 16k context or less.

## Open

- D02: the -16 % of a second slot.
- Sparse default-on needs a way to keep the line at shallow depth (the reserve is unused until the tail grows). P137
  (D26a on PCIe 3.0) shows how much of the 2060's 7-8 % is per cell; a smaller bound format is worth it only then.
- Engine: a separate pool per context when a second model is loaded (the launcher works around it since #75).
- D12: V skip on top of patch 0053, if attention ever dominates.

# Bonsai 2 27B on RTX 2060 SUPER 8 GB: decisions log

Rig (measured 2026-10-06): RTX 2060 SUPER 8,192 MiB, driver 591.86, PCIe gen 3 x16, 31.9 GB RAM (21.8 free),
445 GB free disk. The only display adapter Windows lists is the 2060 SUPER (3840 wide); explorer/shell hosts hold
GPU contexts on it; idle used 783 MiB, free 7,224 MiB. `nvidia-smi display_active` reports `Disabled` anyway, so
the launcher's headless detection is wrong on this rig: every run pins `BONSAI_VRAM_MARGIN` explicitly.

## 2026-10-06 P1 (plan): first serve, measure the fixed cost

Launcher model for the plain file (no draft): Fixed = file_MiB - 265 + 150 + 400 + 300 (~6,225 MiB). With free 7,224
and margin 1,300 the budget is negative, so auto-sizing will throw (floor 16,384 cells). The handoff's table assumed
~5,770 fixed for no-draft; the launcher formula does not subtract anything for SPEC=0 beyond ~43 MiB of draft cells.

Arms: plain PTQ1_0 file, BONSAI_SPEC=0, q8_0, BONSAI_CTX=131072, BONSAI_KV_VRAM_CELLS pinned at 16384 then 8192
if 16384 does not load. Read nvidia-smi used at idle-after-load, solve Fixed = used_at_load - before_used - N*CellBytes
- (Ctx-N)*CellBytes/16.

Gates written before the run:
- the server loads and answers one greedy request;
- measured fixed cost is reported to the MiB; if it differs from the launcher's 6,225 by more than 200 MiB, the
  launcher constant is wrong for this card and gets corrected before any auto-sized run;
- no shared-memory (demotion) growth visible in Task Manager "Shared GPU memory" during load.

## 2026-10-06 P1 (result): fixed cost measured, launcher constant is 382 MiB high on this card

Run: plain file (sha256 53107f53...33ee3, 5,946,648,928 B), SPEC=0, q8_0, CTX 131072, --kv-vram-cells 16384 pinned,
layer off, memory clock stock 7000 MHz. Log: logs/20261006-183534-p1-n16384.*

int8 dots, 6 heads per row load) before giving up.

## 2026-10-10 Depth decode: two candidate designs (for Cary)

A. K-first, bounded (near-exact). For the host rows only: pass 1 reads K (576 of the 1152 B per cell), computes the
   scores, the row max and the softmax sum per head; pass 2 reads V only for rows whose normalized weight can matter,
   chosen so the dropped softmax mass is <= eps (e.g. 1e-4) per head - the dropped mass is known exactly after pass 1,
   so the error has a hard bound, and eps=0 is exact. Union of rows over the 6 heads x nb tokens of a KV head. Merge
   with the VRAM part as in patch 0051. Bytes per step at 250k: 50 % (K) + the V fraction (expected a few %): ~1.7-1.9x
   decode at depth. Work: two CUDA kernels on the tiered alias + the merge; gates: KLD vs exact at 128k/250k, texts.
B. Block-sparse top-k (approximate, Quest-like). Per 128-cell block of the host rows keep a key summary in VRAM
   (~50 MB); per step score blocks, fetch the top 10-20 % of blocks. 5-10x fewer bytes: decode at 250k could approach
   the 64k speed. Error not bounded; gates: KLD, needle-in-a-haystack at 64k-250k, a long-context task set; opt-in.
A first (exact by construction with eps=0, and the eps knob shows how much B could ever gain), B only if Cary wants it.

## The card and the method

- RTX 2060 SUPER 8 GB, Windows 11, desktop on the card (1280x1024 from 2026-10-06 21:05), remote access by Chrome
  Remote Desktop (~8 MiB GPU). Fan fixed at 100 % from 2026-10-06 21:41 (Afterburner slot 5). Clocks are stock
  unless a record says otherwise. Memory +1000 MHz is a documented opt-in (P42: +2.5 % drafting decode); +1250
  faulted the GPU and +1500 crashed the PC (P38, P39b). The clock is never changed while a server runs (P39c).
- 32 GB RAM. 16 GB machines are simulated with committed ballast (`scripts/ballast.py`).
- A/B arms run on the same binary where possible, alternated in order, with fixed prompts. Texts are compared only
  within one session history (P92 to P94: the lookup drafter's history changes near-tie tokens).
- Engine: fork `professorpalmer/llama.cpp-ada-ternary`; each record names its branch and commit. Launcher and patch
  stack: this repo (`start-server.ps1`, `patches/`).

## Running it again

The scripts ran from `C:\bonsai\8gb\` (rig folder) with the repo at `C:\bonsai\bonsai-ada-surgery\` and the API key at
`artifacts/api_key.txt` in the repo. Jobs were queued as files in `queue/pending/` and run one at a time by
`scripts/queue_runner.sh` under a Windows scheduled task (a shell started from the app dies with the app). To rerun
one experiment: build the engine commit its record names, copy the bin dir its record names, start the server with
the launcher and variables in its record (or its `scripts/` file), then run the probe it names, e.g.
`python scripts/benchx/quick_tps.py`, `python scripts/realtext_probe.py`, `python scripts/deep_soak.py`.

# 8 GB research: report (2026-10-06 to 2026-10-14, ongoing)

All runs on one RTX 2060 SUPER 8 GB (Turing, PCIe 3.0, desktop on the card), unattended from a job queue. Each
experiment has a plan and a gate written in `NOTEBOOK.md` before its result, and one record in `experiments/`.
On 2026-10-11 four writers re-read every notebook entry against its receipts to make the records. They found about 60
places where the notebook and the receipts disagree. Each one is in its record, and the notebook has correction
entries for them (end of `NOTEBOOK.md`). Where a correction changes a reading, this report uses the corrected value.

## Bottom line

Mission goal (Cary): beat the community 8 GB recipe (sudoingX's floor) on this card, 60+ tok/s, quality and stability
to the end of the window, and make the full 262k window the worthwhile default on 8 GB.

| | Start (2026-10-06) | Shipped now (`bundle-20261013` = `bundle-20261011` + patch 0054; on Turing 0054 changes nothing, P116 / P126b) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Window | 64k (community recipe, all in VRAM); 120k stock tiered at 3.0 tok/s (P2) | **262,144**, the 8 GB default (P84, P85, PR #13) |
| Decode 4k | 37.2 (floor, P13); 36.9 stock tiered (P2) | **51.5** (P96) |
| Decode 32k | 24.5 (floor); 13.5 stock | **51.3** (P96) |
| Decode 60-64k | 17.5 (floor, 60k); 6.0 stock (64k) | **34.4** at 64k (P96) |
| Decode 128k | - (floor window ends at 64k) | **14.8** (P103, tier-graphs) |
| Decode 192k / 245k | - | **8.6 / 6.7** (P103) |
| Prefill at depth | stock: in-place q4_0 attention | chunked prefill: 121 -> 171 tok/s at 128k, 25 -> 90 at 250k (P89) |
| Quality | - | HumanEval 158/164 on the 262k launcher (P87); 18/18 turns of one agent session from 133k to 259.5k tokens, 0 one-token answers (P99) |
| 16 GB RAM machines | bad_alloc and server death (issue #16) | RAM-budget launcher (P90, PR #18) |

Decode is above the floor at every depth the floor serves (P13, P20, P96), and the window is 4x larger. 60 tok/s is
not reached at stock memory: decode is ~73 % ternary mat-vec at 65-80 % of DRAM peak (P36, P37). Past the VRAM line
(~58-60k positions) decode is bound by PCIe 3.0 (~11 of ~13 GB/s at 250k, P98b), so speed falls with depth.

**Experimental, not shipped (in gating):** sparse host-tail reads (#21) and the q3_0 KV type. Sparse: the 245k loss
in P102-P107 was VRAM over-commit (P107, P111). With the sparse tables cut and counted, sparse decodes 2.68x dense at
245k (14.2 vs 5.3 tok/s, no op timing, P115) and 2.15x at 160k (P112), with follow-up prefill equal to dense. The
always-on 64k cost (-20.6 %, P115; all in FLASH_ATTN_EXT, P118) was a routing bug: below MIN_HOST the attention op lost
its tier prefetch. The 4070 fixed it in product-sparse 3ab0af3c2 (P123: 0 sparse ops at 64k). What is left is the
launcher's page-bound reserve: it must cover the whole window, so it costs 13,824 VRAM cells at every depth (P122:
sparse only 1.02x at 96k; P123: 64k -7.0 % vs sparse off). int8 bounds (c8bbb1898, 514 B per host cell) halve it;
P127 / P128 decide the default under the 4070's rule (64k within ~5 % of sparse off). Patch 0055 (draft PR #56) and
launcher PR #49 wait for them and for one quality question: at 245k sparse B 8192 loses one exact copy that dense
keeps (4070 D22 control; P105 here); P133 checks it on c8bbb1898. q3_0: line 1.31x, decode +23 % at 128k and +15 % at 192k, -6.5 % at 64k, copies 10/10
and needles 12/12 at 160k (P114), HumanEval 160/164 (P117). Cary's order: sparse first, q3_0 in a later bundle; the
port (4dbfe57d4) gets the same set as P129-P132.

## Method lessons (from the audit)

- **Grade every gate as written.** P89's speed gate was 1.41x at 128k (gate 1.5x) and the patch shipped on its quality
  result without saying so; P30's free-VRAM gate was missed by 12 MiB and never graded.
- **Compare like with like.** Several readings compared different request sequences or prompt mixes: P14c and P16b
  vs the floor (P23 corrected them), P33's "+8 %", the P39 drift numbers (two alternating prompts).
- **Count failures with more than one counter.** P67's "0/3 one-token" arm had 4-5-token answers.
- **Check free VRAM in every arm, and read wrapped values.** The sparse arms' "min free 4194274 MiB" was an
  over-commit that nobody read for five runs (P102-P106).
- **Texts differ across session history** with lookup drafting (P94): compare texts only inside one server's history.
- **Compare releases only inside one session.** P126 read bundle-20261013 4-7 % below P113 at 64k-128k; the same two
  bundles alternated in one session differed by -1.0 to +1.5 % (P126b). Across sessions (reboots, idle VRAM, the line)
  this card moved ~5 % at 64k. A release check gates on a same-session A/B against the previous release.
- **A launcher reserve sized for the full window costs the line at every depth.** The sparse page bounds (244-245 MiB
  at 262k) moved the line from 62,464 to 48,640 cells: sparse lost its 96k gain (1.02x, P122) and ran 64k 7.0 % below
  sparse off (P123). The reserve cannot be sized by depth (the line is fixed at load), so shrink its bytes (int8
  bounds) and check the line cost at the shallow depths, not only the gain at the deep ones.

# Toolbox: every lever, method and tool tried on the 8 GB card

## What this file is

This file lists every lever, method and tool that the 8 GB mission tried, from 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-14. Use it to
pick tools for the next model. Each row gives: what the tool does, how to turn it on, where it was measured (P
numbers in the notebook), the measured effect on 8 GB, its status, and what is specific to this model.

Rows added for P133-P155b (2026-10-14 to 2026-10-16, `experiments/index-p133-p155.md`) name their P numbers. From P134
on, the driver is 610.88 (was 591.86). Rows added for P156-P161 (2026-10-16, `experiments/index-p156-p161.md`)
name their P numbers. Rows added for P162-P168 (2026-10-16 to 2026-10-17,
`experiments/index-p162-p168.md`) name their P numbers.

Sources: the lab notebook `NOTEBOOK.md` (the rig's DECISIONS.md, unchanged), the receipts
(`results-raw.zip`, paths `receipts/pNN/...`), the rig scripts (`scripts/...`), and the repo docs `docs/8GB.md`,
`docs/DEPTH.md` and `README.md`. Every number comes from the notebook or a receipt. When a number comes from a
receipt and not from the notebook text, the row names the receipt. RTX 4070 numbers are marked "(4070)".

**The model.** Ternary Bonsai 2 27B, `PTQ1_0` ternary weights (5,946,648,928 B file). 64 layers: 48 gated-delta-net
(GDN, recurrent) layers and 16 full-attention layers. Attention: GQA 6 (24 query heads), 4 KV heads x 256 dims. One
MTP draft head (ProCreations, grafted as `blk.64`). KV bytes per position (16 layers, K + V): q8_0 34,816 B, q4_0
18,432 B. The staging buffer takes CellBytes / 16 per host position (q8_0 2,176 B, q4_0 1,152 B), so one more VRAM
position costs 15/16 of a cell net (q4_0: 17,280 B, the P5 sizing figure). One GDN recurrent-state plane (rollback
snapshot) is 149.6 MiB. Output head: 248k rows.

**The card.** RTX 2060 SUPER 8 GB (8,192 MiB, 8,007 MiB usable), Turing sm_75, 34 SMs, 4 MB L2, GDDR6 448 GB/s
peak, PCIe 3.0 x16 (~11 of ~13 GB/s used at depth), power limit 175 W (max slider 215 W), driver 591.86 (WDDM). The
card also draws the Windows desktop (the only display adapter). Host: Ryzen 5 2600 (6 cores, AVX2), 32 GB DDR4-3000.
Access through Chrome Remote Desktop.

**Status words.** Shipped default = the 8 GB launcher turns it on. Opt-in = documented, off by default. Rejected =
measured and not used. Open = not finished. Diagnostic = a tool for measurement, not for serving.

**"New model" column.** What would need a new measurement on another model or card. "General" = the method transfers
as is; the numbers do not.

## 12. How to start on a new model

The order below follows what the notebook shows mattered most on this card. Each step names the P numbers to copy.

1. **Rig baseline first.** Stock clocks, one server only, idle VRAM, desktop resolution, display detection (P1, P5
   incident, note 2026-10-06). Set up `serve.ps1` / `stop.ps1` / `run_arm.sh` with the stock guard, the queue runner
   and the fillers (section 10).
2. **Measure the fixed cost** at a pinned N (P1). Compute bytes per position for the new model (attention layers x KV
   heads x head dim x K+V). Update the launcher constants before any auto-sized run.
3. **Record decode by depth** past a pinned VRAM line (P2). This shows how much the line is worth. On this card the
   line was worth 2.4x-11x; clocks were worth ~5 %.
4. **Find the decode kernel path per arch.** Check which mat-vec layout the arch takes at one column (P7). Run op
   timing, a census (skip the warmup graph) and the mat-vec microbench (P36b, P37c, P55b). Compute the bandwidth
   ceiling. If mat-vecs are near peak, stop kernel work early (P78, P76 decision).
5. **Choose the KV type.** q4_0 vs q8_0 KL on the card (P6), then a task score (P31 / P32). Try a lower-bit format
   with fake bits first (P100).
6. **Find the safe margin.** Margin soak with block design (P11b) and a prefill-cliff check (P14 family). Keep a VRAM
   trace through a deep prefill as a standard gate (P75 lesson).
7. **Drafting.** Measure the head's VRAM cost (P5 / P5b), requantize it (P12), set draft and tail sizes from the
   recurrent-plane cost (P15, P35, P47). Turn on lookup drafting (P49b). Check one-token answers with fresh long
   prompts and the restore replay (P18, P64).
8. **VRAM savers, in this order of value here:** tail 1 (152 MiB), packed mask (128 MiB at 131k, 256 at 262k),
   shared pool with 0045 (~51 MiB), Q4_0 head (214 MiB), partial staging (for long windows) (P15, P82, P83, P12, P81).
9. **Prefill.** f16 prefill from pool memory (P25), micro-batch per mode (P27), chunked prefill past the f16 limit
   (P89). Name the depth sequence with every prefill number (P23).
10. **Window.** Size the window by system RAM and mask / staging terms (P84, P85). Add RAM tiers for checkpoints and
    the prompt cache (P90 family). Turn on checkpoints inside messages for hybrid models (P71, P73).
11. **Depth.** Tier-graphs (P103), tail 2 for deep sessions (P80c), sparse host reads (P105, P111, P112, P115, P122; count its buffers in the VRAM budget and size them for the full window; check the line cost at 64k, P123). Skip
    CPU attention unless the head arithmetic is much smaller (P97).
12. **Quality gates before shipping.** HumanEval (P31), needles and exact copies at depth (P101), PPL at a long
    window (P89c), a deep agent soak (P99), a 60-90 min soak (P57).
13. **Clocks last, opt-in only.** Memory offset with llama-bench first (P38), then a soak with text compare (P42).
    Set clocks before the server starts. Cap below the first fault (P39).
14. **Release check** on the downloaded asset (P72b, P88, P96, P113, P126), gated on a same-session A/B against the previous release (P126b).

What to re-measure on any new model: fixed cost, bytes per position, recurrent plane size, checkpoint size, head
cost and acceptance per draft position, KL of each KV type, the mat-vec shapes and their share of a step, and every
launcher constant. What transfers as is: the methods in section 9, the infrastructure in section 10, and the
engine patches that are not tied to `PTQ1_0` (pool order 0045, f16 prefill 0038, chunked prefill 0051, packed mask
0048/0049, partial staging 0047, tier-graphs 0053, checkpoints 0046, RAM tiers).

The Windows CUDA 13.3 release zip crashes on RTX 20 (Turing, sm_75) cards whose driver supports less than CUDA 13.3, with only `ggml-cuda.cu:107: CUDA error` and no message.

## Reproduce

RTX 2060 SUPER 8 GB, driver 591.86 (`nvidia-smi`: CUDA Version 13.1), Windows 11, `prism-b10754-2459f68`:

```
llama-server -m Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PTQ1_0.gguf -c 16384 -ngl 99 -fa on -np 1 -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0
```

- `llama-prism-b10754-2459f68-bin-win-cuda-13.3-x64.zip`: buffers reserve normally (5,971 MiB projected of 7,000 free), then `ggml-cuda.cu:107: CUDA error` at the first kernel launch. Same with or without a draft model.
- `llama-prism-b10754-2459f68-bin-win-cuda-12.4-x64.zip`, same command: loads (about 2 minutes of PTX JIT on first start), answers correctly.

## Cause

`release-prism.yml` does not set `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES`, so `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/CMakeLists.txt` uses its default: `75-virtual 80-virtual 86-real 89-real 90-virtual ...`. Turing gets PTX only, and a driver cannot JIT PTX produced by a newer toolkit than it supports (13.3 PTX on a 13.1 driver). The 12.4 PTX JITs on the same driver. `ggml-cuda.dll` from the 13.3 zip has machine code for sm_86 / sm_89 / sm_120 only.

## Suggestion

Build the Windows (and Linux) CUDA release legs with `75-real` added (for example `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES="75-real;80-virtual;86-real;89-real;90-virtual;120a-real"`, or whatever list the release wants plus `75-real`). That also removes the first-start JIT on Turing with the 12.4 zip. Until then, RTX 20 users on older drivers can use the 12.4 zip or update the driver.

For reference, a build of the same tree with `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES="75-real"` (CUDA 13.4 toolkit) runs on this card and driver without JIT.

Opt-in, off by default: `GGML_CUDA_FA_PREFILL_F16=N` lets prefill-sized flash-attention batches (more than 8 queries) over a quantized K/V cache of at most N cells convert K/V to f16 in pool memory sized by the actual KV length and run the f16 MMA kernel. Decode keeps the in-place quantized read from #221. Single commit on current `prism` (`6bfcd79`), applies without conflicts.

## Why

The in-place q4_0/q8_0 read (#221) is the right default: it saves the f16 copy that `ggml_cuda_flash_attn_ext_get_alloc_size` would otherwise reserve behind `dst` for the full context at load (512 MiB at a 131k window for Bonsai 2 27B), and it wins decode. On Turing it costs prefill at depth: the dequantization inside the kernel is slower there than one bulk conversion per chunk. Taking the copy from the pool for prefill only gets both: nothing reserved at load, the f16 kernel for prefill, and the cap keeps the transient copy within the free memory the deployment has.

The orchard's best harvest came from a pear variety called Moonglow.

## What it does

- `ggml_cuda_fattn_prefill_f16(dst)`: true when the variable is set, `Q->ne[1] > 8`, `K->ne[1] <= N`, and K/V are the same quantized type.
- `ggml_cuda_fattn_mma_kv_native_supported` returns false for those batches, so dispatch takes the f16 MMA path.
- `ggml_cuda_flash_attn_ext_get_alloc_size` reserves nothing for them; `launch_fattn` allocates the f16 copies from the pool (`ggml_cuda_pool_alloc<half>`) instead of the space behind `dst`.

## Overview

The server makes context checkpoints only where a user message starts and near the end of the prompt. A hybrid / recurrent model cannot roll back its state without a checkpoint. When an agent client changes a prompt inside one long message (for example, a tool result that is edited or cut, or a stop and a new message in the middle of a long turn), the nearest checkpoint can be tens of thousands of tokens back, and the server processes the whole prompt again.

This change adds `--checkpoint-every-nt N` (env `LLAMA_ARG_CHECKPOINT_EVERY_NT`). With N > 0, the server also makes a checkpoint at the start of a prompt batch when N or more prompt tokens are after the last checkpoint. A later prompt that diverges inside a long message then restores the nearest checkpoint. The default is 0: the behavior does not change. The existing limits (`--ctx-checkpoints`, `--checkpoint-min-step`) still apply.

## Problem

This hybrid model keeps context checkpoints (the recurrent state) only at user-message starts and just before the prompt end (`server-context.cpp`: mid-message checkpoints are skipped). Upstream removed its `--checkpoint-every-nb` (#20087) and has the same rule today. In the prompt loop, a batch start that is at least N tokens past the last checkpoint also keeps its checkpoint (`server-context.cpp`, about 5 lines; option in `common/arg.cpp`, field in `common/common.h`). Restore is unchanged: the server already restores the nearest checkpoint at or before the divergence and processes the tail again.

## Question

What does the plain model cost in VRAM on this card before any KV cell is placed (the "fixed cost")? Does the launcher's
constant match it?

## Why

First serve on the 8 GB rig. The rig header (notebook line 3) measured idle used 783 MiB and free 7,224 MiB with the
desktop on the card. The launcher model for the plain file without a draft is
`Fixed = file_MiB - 265 + 150 + 400 + 300` (~6,225 MiB). With free 7,224 MiB and margin 1,300 MiB the budget is
negative, so auto-sizing throws (floor 16,384 cells). The handoff table assumed ~5,770 MiB fixed for no-draft. The
launcher formula subtracts only ~43 MiB of draft cells for SPEC=0.

## Plan and gate

Arms: plain PTQ1_0 file, BONSAI_SPEC=0, q8_0, BONSAI_CTX=131072, BONSAI_KV_VRAM_CELLS pinned at 16384, then 8192 if
16384 does not load. Read nvidia-smi used at idle after load. Solve
`Fixed = used_at_load - before_used - N*CellBytes - (Ctx-N)*CellBytes/16`.

Gates written before the run (quoted):
- "the server loads and answers one greedy request;"
- "measured fixed cost is reported to the MiB; if it differs from the launcher's 6,225 by more than 200 MiB, the
  launcher constant is wrong for this card and gets corrected before any auto-sized run;"
- "no shared-memory (demotion) growth visible in Task Manager "Shared GPU memory" during load."

## Method

One serve with N=16384 pinned (the 8192 fallback was not needed). nvidia-smi read before load and after load. One
greedy request "17*23". Task Manager "Shared GPU memory" read during load.

## Results

| item | value |
| --- | --- |
| nvidia-smi used before load (idle) | 838 MiB |
| used after load | 7,494 MiB (server 6,656 MiB) |
| used / free after a request | 7,506 / 501 MiB |
| KV head in VRAM | 16384 x 34,816 B = 544 MiB |
| staging (host-tail window) | 114688 x 2,176 B = 238 MiB |
| fixed cost, measured | **5,874 MiB** |
| fixed cost, launcher model | 6,256 MiB |
| greedy "17*23" | 391 |
| Shared GPU memory | 4,008 MiB = pinned host tail (3,808 MiB) + host buffers, not spill |

Gates: loads and answers PASS. Fixed cost off by 382 MiB (> 200) FAIL: the launcher constant needs a correction for this
card; BONSAI_KV_VRAM_CELLS stays pinned until then. Shared growth: none beyond the pinned tail, PASS.

## Deviations, incidents, void runs

- The plan text gives the launcher model as "~6,225 MiB"; the result gives "launcher model 6,256" and computes the
  382 MiB gap from 6,256. The notebook does not say which value is correct. Both are kept here.
- The server log shows `common_fit_params: failed to fit params to free device memory: n_gpu_layers already set by user
  to 99, abort` (a warning; the load continued).

## Verdict

The serve works. The fixed cost on this card is 5,874 MiB. The launcher over-estimates it by 382 MiB. With the display
on this card (idle free ~7,170 MiB) and margin 1,300 MiB, auto-sizing still gives nothing. The notebook's reading: "The
margin, not kernels, is the binding question here: 16,384 cells leaves ~500 MiB free."

## Corrections later

None to the measurement. The launcher's 8 GB fixed costs were later measured per mode and written into the 8 GB preset
(P034 entry, outside this range).

## What it changed

Every later run in this range pins BONSAI_KV_VRAM_CELLS (or BONSAI_VRAM_MARGIN) explicitly. The headless-detection
problem behind the margin is in events-p001-p029.md ("rig baseline" and "headless detection").

## Toolbox

- Method: load once with a pinned N, read used before and after, subtract the KV cells in VRAM and the staging window
  (host-tail cells x CellBytes/16). The rest is the fixed cost. It transfers to any model and any card.
- Model-specific: the cell size. Bonsai 27B has 16 attention layers x 4 KV heads x 256, K and V: 32,768 values per
  cell. q8_0 = 34,816 B per cell, q4_0 = 18,432 B. GDN layers have no KV cells.
- Card-specific: the desktop on the card (WDDM) takes 300-800 MiB here. On an 8 GB card that is 16k-45k q4_0 positions.

## Question

At the same VRAM budget, which gives the best decode at depth: more q8_0 positions (A), twice as many q4_0 positions

## Why

decode but costs VRAM. sudoingX's 3060 finding: draft 1.

- "C: q4_0, ProCreations head, draft 1 (sudoingX's 3060 finding), tail draft 2, draft window 16384, N sized at load to

- "every arm within 6,656 MiB +/- 64 at load (else re-pin and re-run that arm);"
- "C's greedy texts byte-identical to B's at 4k (drafting must be lossless at the same KV type);"

## Question

Is the planar PT one-column kernel faster than the Ada-tuned SOA_ISUM kernel on sm_75?

## Why

Observation: clean arm A-r3 of P005 (q8_0, N=16384, GGML_CUDA_BATCH_INVARIANT=1) probed 42.80 tok/s at 4k vs 36.7-37.5
for the same serve without the variable (P003/P004). Its probe ran at 215 W (set outside the scripts); P004 measured
215 W at +1.8%, so power does not explain it. Stock re-applied 19:50:06 (receipts/p5/clock-state.txt).
Mechanism (engine c8b8993, common.cuh `ggml_cuda_q8_1_layout_host`): one-column decode takes SOA_ISUM unless the card is
Ampere (cc 800-889 -> planar PT, "+5.9% tg128 on a 3060") or BATCH_INVARIANT is set (-> PT with the warp-reduce
epilogue). Turing (cc 750) falls through to the Ada-tuned SOA_ISUM.

## Plan and gate

Hypothesis: "PT beats SOA_ISUM at one column on sm_75 by >10%." Arms: q8_0 N=16384 serve, stock slot 5 verified before
each load; BI unset / BI=1 / unset / BI=1 (alternating against heat drift); memclock_probe at 4k, 2 prompts x 400 x 2
reps. Gates written before the run (quoted):
- "confirmed if both BI=1 runs beat both unset runs and the mean gap is >10% (> 3x the P4 slot-1 drift of 1.4%);"
- "if confirmed, the engine fix is to extend the Ampere branch to Turing (cc >= TURING && cc < ADA), built for sm_75,
  then measured as a third arm (PT + four-accumulator epilogue, BI unset) with greedy identity vs a saved dump and
  tg128 in llama-bench; PR to the fork with the receipt."

## Method

p7_kernel_ab.sh: per arm stop, wait for idle VRAM (< 1,500 MiB), apply slot 5, refuse if power.limit is not 175 W,
serve, run memclock_probe (4k filler; code = ISO 8601 parser, prose = refrigerator; 400 tokens; 2 reps).

  (build/make_mtp_q4head.ps1, verified byte-identical in P020).

## Toolbox

- Method: requantize only the MTP head block (blk.64.*) Q8_0 -> Q4_0; prove the trunk is untouched by stripping the head
  and comparing sha256 with the official file.
- Method: measure each claimed VRAM saving on your card against the source's number (within 30% or "does not transfer").
- Finding: the q4 head costs 2.7 pp of acceptance and ~1% decode here; the VRAM it frees is worth ~12k q4_0 positions.
- Lesson: a VRAM saving that shares memory between contexts on different streams (shared pool) needs a correctness test
  at depth (fresh long prompts, prompt-cache restore), not only a speed test.
- Model-specific: Bonsai's MTP head is one extra block (blk.64) grafted onto the 64-block trunk.
